wire.response: occurrences[]: primary locator, ordered additional locators, unique unary functions[]
wire.locator: atom handle plus either no boundaries for a whole atom, or range-validated A#:B# from/to coordinate encodings for a strict span

validation.atomHandle: must be present in the request-local owned atom domain
validation.boundaries: must parse to an in-range offset for that atom; strict form requires from < to; a full-atom boundary pair is refused because whole form is canonical handle-only
validation.multipart: additional parts must be owned, strictly source-ordered, and are passed through the existing exact binder
validation.functionSet: unique finite subset; no mutual-exclusion assumption

boundaryAuthority.limitation: A model-authored A#:B# whose offset is in range is accepted even if that exact boundary was not separately issued by the request. P6C must replace parsing with opaque registry lookup before coarse-domain execution can be qualified.

singletonExactIdentityShard.policy: owner is a complete harness-issued locator identity, including ordered continuation locators; a response admits at most that one locator record.
singletonExactIdentityShard.semanticRestriction: NONE: every exact source identity has a deterministic owner shard; no occurrence/count cap is inferred.
singletonExactIdentityShard.caveat: This establishes a finite safe execution leaf, not an operationally acceptable number of provider calls. Coarser source-domain aggregation requires a separate source-domain-handle and aggregate-volume proof.

metrics.semanticSelectionQuality: future Gold occurrence evaluation over locator-selected identities
metrics.exactBindingQuality: locator decode/binder acceptance and identity equality, reported separately

providerManifest: NOT_PREPARED: P6B is a local contract proof only; no model behavior or practical shard schedule has been qualified.
conclusion: The P6B compact encoding removes copied-text and context-echo representation failures while retaining exact source identity. It is not yet a harness-issued boundary registry. A singleton exact-identity shard fits the response cap without semantic cardinality, but neither opacity nor operational leaf granularity is claimed here.
